phases.name: Slice 01 — delete from the full page: the whole write path on the surface with no board reconciliation
phases.description: Ships the delete PRIMITIVE and the entire vertical behind it, on the surface whose success is a redirect. Bottom-up: the store primitive reds first (it is the seam both other slices consume), then the service use cases, then the handlers and templates. No slice-02 or slice-03 step may start until 01's issue_delete::delete_issues_with_outbox signature exists. ZERO migrations — the schema head stays 0015 (DDD-11); the cascade FKs (0004/0005/0013) and the outbox table already ship. Slice 01 leaves lanes.rs untouched: rewiring the lane fate is slice 03 (DDD-2).

steps.name: The store primitive: issue_delete::delete_issues_with_outbox deletes by id set on the caller's transaction, and Store::delete_issue_with_outbox owns a transaction for one card
criteria: Replaces the panicking scaffold in crates/foundry-store/src/issue_delete.rs with a real implementation carrying the same signature — the signature is DESIGN-pinned (DDD-1/DDD-4) and MUST NOT change: the batch arm takes &mut Transaction so slice 03's lane caller can ride its own.
Performs ZERO lookups: consumes the caller-supplied IssueDeleteContext { workspace_id, project_id, key_prefix } (DDD-3).
Deletes with one DELETE ... WHERE id = ANY($1); comments, attachments and change events go via the schema's ON DELETE CASCADE — NO application-level child delete is written (DDD-11).
Returns rows_affected. Ok(0) is the not-there case and MUST write no outbox row (DDD-10).
The outbox emit is DEFERRED to slice 03: this step writes the DELETE and the return contract only. Emitting here would make slice 03's regression scenarios untestable as a delta.
Removes the SCAFFOLD marker from crates/foundry-store/src/issue_delete.rs.
Removes the dead Store::delete_issue_cascade from crates/foundry-store/src/attachments.rs (zero production callers, verified by grep).

Store-integration coverage: a single delete removes exactly one issues row; its comments/attachments/change events are gone; sibling issues are byte-identical; deleting a non-existent id returns 0 and writes nothing.
steps.scenario_name: delete_issues_with_outbox removes exactly the named rows and cascades their children; a vanished id returns 0 and writes nothing; siblings are untouched
steps.implementation_notes: Unit/integration only — no acceptance scenario is un-pended by this step. It exists because it is the seam slices 02 and 03 consume, and slice 01's learning hypothesis is precisely whether one &mut Transaction-taking primitive serves both owners.

steps.name: The service use cases: delete_issue_dialog reads the advisory counts, delete_issue writes — both behind resolve_member_project
criteria: Replaces the panicking scaffolds in crates/foundry-services/src/issues.rs with real implementations, keeping the DESIGN-pinned signatures (DDD-7).
Both gate on the SHIPPED resolve_member_project — no new authz code is written anywhere in this feature.
Membership, not authorship, is the gate (D2): a member who did not file the issue may delete it.
delete_issue maps a rows_affected of 0 to ServiceError::NotFound so the handler renders the uniform 404 (DDD-10); Forbidden stays Forbidden.
delete_issue_dialog returns IssueDeleteView { key, number, comment_count, attachment_count }. Counts are ADVISORY (D13) — they are read here and never gate the write.
Reuses Store::count_comments_for_issue verbatim; the attachment count is the DESIGN open question 1 — add the symmetric one-line store method rather than counting a list read.
Removes the SCAFFOLD markers from both functions.

CORRECTED DURING DELIVERY: an earlier draft of this criterion said to ADD Store::count_attachments_for_issue. It already ships at crates/foundry-store/src/attachments.rs:168 (slice 3, commit b2475f6) with exactly the symmetric body described. Adding it would have been a duplicate inherent-impl method and would not have compiled. Reuse it verbatim. This step therefore adds ZERO new store surface and leaves crates/foundry-store/src/lib.rs untouched — DESIGN open question 1 is answered by reuse, not by a new method.
steps.scenario_name: delete_issue refuses a non-member with Forbidden and a vanished issue with NotFound; a member who is not the author succeeds; delete_issue_dialog returns live advisory counts
steps.implementation_notes: The attachment-count store method is the only NEW store surface here; everything else reuses shipped reads.

steps.name: The confirm dialog and its two carriers: delete_issue_modal.html plus the delete_issue_modal_page.html no-JS wrapper
criteria: Creates crates/foundry-app/templates/partials/delete_issue_modal.html mirroring delete_lane_modal.html's contract: bare fragment for #modal-root, data-modal="delete-issue", [data-action="close-modal"] as the ONLY close, hidden _csrf, [data-error-slot], and the shipped 'this cannot be undone' sentence (D3).

The copy COUNTS consequences rather than warning: it names the issue key and states how many comments and attachments go with it; it branches for the zero-consequence case exactly as delete_lane_modal.html branches on card_count == 0 (DESIGN open question 3).

Creates crates/foundry-app/templates/delete_issue_modal_page.html which {% extends "base.html" %} and {% include %}s that SAME partial — one body, two carriers, so the fragment and the page can never disagree (DDD-6).
Adds IssueDeleteModal and IssueDeleteModalPage view models to crates/foundry-app/src/views.rs.
Any new CSS lands in the content-hashed stylesheet using --cz-* tokens only, with static/VENDOR.md updated in the SAME commit; `cargo xtask check-arch` must stay green.
steps.scenario_name: The confirm names the issue and counts what goes with it; The confirm says so when nothing goes with the issue

steps.name: The handlers and the full-page Delete control: the happy path — a card is removed and its children go with it
criteria: Replaces the 501 scaffolds in crates/foundry-app/src/issues.rs with real handlers and removes the __SCAFFOLD__ markers from their bodies.
show_delete_form serves the bare fragment for #modal-root on the htmx path, minting/reusing the CSRF cookie exactly as show_edit_form does. The direct-navigation carrier is step 01-06.
submit_delete answers 303 to the board on the non-htmx path (D8) — never a re-render of a page for a resource that no longer exists.
Adds the Delete control to crates/foundry-app/templates/issue.html beside the <h1> as an hx-get into #modal-root.
Membership, not authorship, is the gate (D2) — a card filed by another member deletes cleanly.
The advisory counts do not gate: a comment filed between the dialog GET and the confirm POST goes with the issue (D13).
Un-pends the 6 happy-path @us-icd-01 scenarios one at a time; each must be GREEN before the next is un-pended.
steps.scenario_name: Confirming removes the card and returns her to the board; Everything hanging off the card goes with it; The cards beside it are untouched; Deleting a card is not a change to the board's lanes; A card filed by someone else can be deleted by any team member; A comment filed while the confirmation is open goes with the issue
steps.implementation_notes: The routes are ALREADY mounted by the DISTILL scaffold — this step changes handler bodies, not the route table. Do not re-register.

steps.name: The refusal surface: every way to be told no is byte-identical to a card that never existed
criteria: Refusals on BOTH verbs map through the shipped idiom: Forbidden -> non_member_page, NotFound -> resource_not_found_page. No key is echoed in ANY branch (DDD-9).

A non-member, a signed-out caller, an already-deleted card and a never-filed card all receive the SAME uniform non-enumerable 404 — a refusal must not be distinguishable by status OR by body (ADR-003).
The double-submit race collapses into the same path: rows_affected of 0 -> NotFound, and NO outbox row (DDD-10).
A POST without a valid token is refused by the SHIPPED csrf_middleware before the handler runs — by route registration alone, with no per-route work (ADR-009).

Un-pends the 6 refusal @us-icd-01 scenarios. The signed-out and tokenless ones are already GREEN against the scaffold (see distill/red-classification.md) and must STAY green — they are regression guards, not new assertions.
steps.scenario_name: Deleting a card on a board she is not a member of is refused indistinguishably; A non-member is refused at the confirmation as well as at the delete; A signed-out delete is refused the same way; Deleting a card that is already gone is refused indistinguishably; Deleting a card that never existed is refused the same way; A delete that carries no token is refused before anything is written
steps.implementation_notes: The refusal oracle asserts the uniform 404 AND byte-identity against a verb-matched never-existed path. Byte-identity alone was vacuous at RED (both sides returned the same scaffold 501) — see distill/red-classification.md.

steps.name: The scripting-disabled path: the no-JS carrier and the plain href fallback
criteria: show_delete_form branches on is_htmx: a DIRECT navigation renders delete_issue_modal_page (the base.html carrier from 01-03), not the bare fragment (DDD-6).
The issue.html Delete control carries a plain href alongside its hx-get, so it is followable with scripting off (D6, AC-1.11).
The confirm page's form is a plain <form method="post">; its POST redirects to the board.

Asserting the route merely answers 200 is NOT sufficient — the browser scenario follows a real <a href> and asserts a real page with the site's own chrome, because a 200 would pass over exactly the bare floating fragment ADR-ISSUE-DELETE-002 rejected.
Un-pends the two @needs-browser scripting-disabled scenarios.
steps.scenario_name: The whole path works with scripting switched off; The confirmation is a readable page when scripting is switched off
steps.implementation_notes: Runs in the @needs-browser lane, which the DEFAULT lane excludes — verify with the `all` lane or FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=icd, never the default lane alone.

phases.name: Slice 02 — delete from the popup, board refreshes in place
phases.description: Pure adapter work on slice 01's proven port. Adds the popup control and the out-of-band #board-columns success response. Depends on slice 01's delete_issue use case; adds no store or service surface.

steps.name: The popup's Delete control, rendered OUTSIDE the edit form
criteria: Adds a Delete control to crates/foundry-app/templates/partials/issue_edit_modal.html placed OUTSIDE the <form> element, beside the ×, carrying data-action="delete-issue" and an hx-get of the confirm route into #modal-root (D5).

Placement is a MARKUP contract asserted as DOM containment, not styling — the control must not be a descendant of the edit form, inheriting the protection adr-modal-close-001 D-12 established for the close trigger.

Writes NO JavaScript: the control is attributes only, resolved by the existing delegated listeners, so keyboard.js keeps its exactly-one-keydown / exactly-one-click budget and BR-4 holds by construction.
The shipped edit-and-save path is unchanged — its regression scenario stays green.

The AC-2.8 regression scenario 'Saving an edit from the card's dialog still works exactly as before' is green BEFORE and AFTER this step — it is the guard that the new control did not disturb the shipped save path.
steps.scenario_name: The card's own dialog offers Delete where it cannot be mistaken for Save; Choosing Delete asks before it acts; Choosing Delete does not save a half-typed edit; Saving an edit from the card's dialog still works exactly as before (regression guard: adding a control outside the form must not disturb the form)

steps.name: The htmx success response: cleared #modal-root plus the out-of-band #board-columns refresh
criteria: submit_delete's htmx arm returns the cleared #modal-root plus the OOB #board-columns refresh through the SHIPPED partials/oob/board_columns_oob.html (D7) — the exact shape lane-delete success already returns.
Both arms call the SAME issue_service::delete_issue: one use case, two renderings (AC-2.9).
After the refresh the board renders every surviving card in its original lane and order, and each column still offers all six lane operations — the OOB refresh must not desync the ⋯ menu (AC-2.5).
Un-pends the remaining @us-icd-02 scenarios, including the @needs-browser real-browser CSRF one (AC-2.7 — proven in a browser, never only over HTTP).

A non-member deleting from the board receives the uniform non-enumerable 404, byte-identical to a card that never existed — the popup path must not become the enumeration oracle the full-page path closed (DDD-9).

BLOCKED THEN CORRECTED (DELIVER, 2026-09-07): two defects in the DISTILL step module, both authored by the orchestrator, stopped this step. (1) `when_deletes_from_page` calls `support::harness::signed_in_post`, which sends COOKIE but NO `HX-Request` header — so both HTTP-lane popup scenarios drove the NON-htmx path while `then_still_on_that_board` and `then_six_lane_ops` asserted an htmx response. The panic text ("the htmx success path must carry...") shows the author believed otherwise. Other step modules build the request manually with `.header("HX-Request", "true")` (feature_issue_edit_dialog.rs:449); this module did not. (2) `when_browser_delete` uses bare `client.find(...)` after two htmx swaps with no wait; fantoccini's `find` does not poll, so the CSRF guard races and cannot reliably reach the submit it exists to click. The house idiom is `client.wait().at_most(...).for_element(...)`.

The crafter was RIGHT to refuse the available workaround: returning the OOB body unconditionally would have greened both scenarios while breaking D8/DDD-6 — the no-JS scenario would then render a bare unstyled fragment and STILL pass, because `then_looking_at_board` accepts any body containing `data-issue-key`. That is exactly the outcome ADR-ISSUE-DELETE-002 rejects, arrived at silently.
steps.scenario_name: Confirming from the board removes the card without leaving the board; The refreshed board keeps every other card and every lane operation; Backing out of the confirmation leaves the card alone; A real browser carries the delete through; A non-member deleting from the board is refused indistinguishably

phases.name: Slice 03 — a deleted card leaves every open board, and lane delete stops being silent
phases.description: Adds the outbox emit to the shared primitive and rewires lanes.rs onto it (DDD-2). This CHANGES SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR: lane delete with fate=delete goes from announcing nothing to announcing N. ADR-BOARD-LANE-002 is amended in ONE clause; this slice is what proves it is one. Slice 02 is NOT a dependency — 03 may land before or after it.

steps.name: The outbox emit inside the primitive's transaction
criteria: delete_issues_with_outbox writes one IssueDeleted outbox row per row ACTUALLY deleted (rows_affected), never one per card requested (DDD-3), inside the caller's transaction so a committed delete can never fail to announce itself and a rolled-back one announces nothing (AC-3.1).

The payload carries project_id, workspace_id, issue_id, number, key and deleted: true, using ONLY fields EventPayload already declares; schema_version stays 1 and NO field is added to crates/foundry-realtime/src/lib.rs (DDD-12, AC-3.2).
key is composed from key_prefix + number BEFORE or DURING the delete — after it there is no row left to compose from. This is slice 03's named risk.
Every refusal path writes ZERO outbox rows (AC-3.7).
steps.scenario_name: The announcement names the card that went; A deleted card leaves a board someone else is looking at; Another project's board hears nothing; A refused delete announces nothing; Comments on other cards still arrive alongside

steps.name: The board's first live-updating surface: a client-side SSE consumer that drops deleted cards
criteria: NEW CAPABILITY, discovered during step 03-01: foundry ships NO client-side SSE consumer. The /events endpoint, the outbox->LISTEN->broadcast->SSE topology and its server-side subscribers are all shipped and green (us-09 8/8), but nothing in static/js/ opens an EventSource and no browser in foundry live-updates anything. The two @needs-browser fan-out scenarios assert behaviour the application cannot produce. The user chose to BUILD it (2026-09-07).

Create crates/foundry-app/static/js/board-live.js — one app-owned vanilla IIFE, matching the house idiom of the five siblings (board-dnd.js, board-lane-dnd.js, csrf-upload.js, keyboard.js, form-errors.js). It opens an EventSource on the board's /team/{team}/project/{project}/events endpoint and, on an IssueDeleted event, removes the matching article.issue-card[data-issue-key] node from the board.

Load it from crates/foundry-app/templates/base.html with `<script src="/static/js/board-live.js" defer></script>`, beside its siblings. App-owned JS is UNHASHED under /static/js/ (only css/foundry.<hash>.css is content-hashed), and takes NO VENDOR.md row — only theme.js has one, because it is a port from canzan-lift and its provenance is the point. Adding a spurious VENDOR row would make check-arch's 'every VENDOR.md sha256 recomputes' rule police a file that needs no provenance claim.

It must no-op safely off the board: base.html serves every page, so the script must find its endpoint from the DOM (or exit early when the board markup is absent) rather than assuming a board context. A thrown exception on the sign-in page would be a regression across the whole app.

It must survive the out-of-band #board-columns refresh. That refresh REPLACES the #board-columns subtree, so anything holding a node reference to a card is left detached — the same class of failure ADR-BOARD-LANE-005 records for the lane menu, which is why that menu stores its open-state in the DOM rather than in a handle. Re-query on each event; do not cache card nodes.
Scope it to IssueDeleted only. The stream already carries CommentAdded, CommentEdited, CommentDeleted and IssueUpdated; this step does not consume them, and must not break on receiving them.
Zero new dependencies, no framework, no bundler — DB6: NO Node, NO package.json, NO minifier, NO CDN at runtime.

Un-pend and green the TWO @needs-browser fan-out scenarios: 'A deleted card leaves a board someone else is looking at' (already un-pended and red from step 03-01 — leave it un-pended) and 'A second board loses every card of a lane that was deleted' (currently @pending; it also needs step 03-03's lane rewiring, so if it cannot green here, re-@pend it and hand it to 03-03 explicitly rather than leaving it red).
steps.scenario_name: A deleted card leaves a board someone else is looking at; A second board loses every card of a lane that was deleted
steps.implementation_notes: This is foundry's FIRST browser-side live-update surface. It is a genuine new capability that arrived through a delete feature because DISCUSS AC-3.4 assumed it existed. It is deliberately scoped to the single event this feature needs; a general live-board is a separate feature and must not be attempted here. Ordered BEFORE 03-03 because the lane rewiring's second-board scenario depends on this consumer existing.

steps.name: Rewire the lane DeleteCards fate onto the shared primitive
criteria: Replaces lanes.rs::delete_cards_permanently's body with a call to issue_delete::delete_issues_with_outbox on the fate's EXISTING transaction, then deletes the now-empty helper (DDD-2).

ADR-BOARD-LANE-002's transaction shape, statement order, last-lane gate, confirm-time membership binding, FK strand-guard and <=3 bounded retry must all come through UNCHANGED. If the rewiring turns out to require restructuring delete_lane_with_fate, that is a finding to RAISE, not work to absorb.
fate=delete on N cards emits exactly N IssueDeleted (AC-3.8).
fate=move still emits exactly N IssueUpdated and ZERO IssueDeleted, and still writes one 0013 status event per card (AC-3.9) — this is what keeps the ADR amendment to one clause.
The shipped board-lane-management and board-lane-overflow-menu scenarios stay green and unmodified (AC-3.10).
Amends docs/product/architecture/adr-board-lane-002 only if DELIVER's measurement contradicts the amendment already recorded there.

Fixes the four comments left stale by step 01-01, which removed Store::delete_issue_cascade while the boundary rules kept 01-01 out of these files: lanes.rs:13, :336 and :340, plus feature_board_lane_management.rs:2075. All four name a function that no longer exists. Three sit in the very block this step rewrites. While there, correct lanes.rs:337-339, which cites migrations 0006/0011/0013 for the cascade FKs — the actual ON DELETE CASCADE declarations are 0004_comments.sql:22, 0005_issue_attachments.sql:19 and 0013_issue_change_events.sql:21 (pre-existing error, surfaced by 01-01).
steps.scenario_name: Emptying a lane by deleting it announces every card that went; Moving a lane's cards still announces them as moved, never as deleted; A lane delete that is refused still announces nothing; A second board loses every card of a lane that was deleted
steps.implementation_notes: Highest-risk step in the feature: it is the only one that edits shipped, working code. Run the full board-lane-management and board-lane-overflow-menu tags before and after.

phases.name: Slice 04 — converge the refusal surface: every authz refusal is the uniform non-enumerable 404
phases.description: USER DECISION (2026-09-06): delete and edit must be equally strict, converging UPWARD. Step 01-05 collapsed the two delete verbs to the uniform 404 because DISCUSS AC-1.8 required it; that left delete stricter than the other 20 authz refusals in the HTML adapter. This phase raises the rest to match. It CHANGES SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR across 5 modules and rewrites two shipped @nfr-sec-06 scenarios, so it is its own phase with its own regression pass.

steps.name: Every non_member_page authz refusal becomes the uniform non-enumerable 404
criteria: Replace every `non_member_page(...)` call site with `resource_not_found_page()` across crates/foundry-app/src/: issues.rs (6 remaining), comments.rs (6), projects.rs (4), attachments.rs (2), keyboard.rs (2). The two delete verbs already converged in step 01-05.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION — do NOT touch CSRF 403s. `csrf_middleware` legitimately answers 403 for a missing/invalid double-submit token, and that is a DIFFERENT refusal from an authz refusal. Shipped scenarios assert it (feature_board_lane_management.rs:1866, feature_b_web_tier.rs:874, and board-lane-reorder's tokenless arm). Every one of those must stay green and unmodified. Conflating the two would be the single worst outcome of this step.

Do NOT touch foundry-api's 403 JSON envelope (`code = "forbidden"`, feature_a_programmatic.rs). The API surface has its own non-enumerability contract and its own author-only authz; it is out of scope.

Update the two shipped @nfr-sec-06 scenarios that assert the OLD behaviour: us-07-project-create.feature 'A workspace member who is not on the team cannot create a project there' and us-08-file-issue.feature 'A workspace member not on the team cannot file an issue against that team's project'. Both currently assert 'the response status is 403 Forbidden'. NFR-SEC-06 requires that the auth check EXISTS and refuses (docs/feature/foundry-backend-mvp/design/auth.md:215, default-deny); the 403 was its exemplar observable, not the requirement. Converging to 404 keeps default-deny and adds non-enumerability. Change the assertion, not the scenario's intent, and keep its @nfr-sec-06 tag.
The whole default acceptance lane must be green afterwards, and the count must be unchanged at 618 — this step un-pends nothing and adds no scenario.

CORRECTED DURING DELIVERY (1): `non_member_page` is NOT one shared helper — it is FIVE module-private copies, one each in issues.rs, comments.rs, projects.rs, attachments.rs and keyboard.rs. All five are deleted once their callers are converted.

CORRECTED DURING DELIVERY (2): the orchestrator's phrase check was incomplete. It grepped only the exact string `the response status is 403 Forbidden` and missed three sibling phrasings, each a non-member authz refusal that must also converge: us-10-comments.feature:95 `Then the response status is 403`; us-11-attachments.feature:78 `Then the upload is refused as forbidden (HTTP 403)`; us-11-attachments.feature:87 `Then the download is refused as forbidden (HTTP 403)`. The us-11 phrases hardcode 403 in the step TEXT, so both the feature text and the step regex change.

NOT converging (verified distinct): us-10-comment-edit-delete.feature:96 stays 403 — it is the author-only edit refusal via `forbidden_fragment`, an authorship rule rather than a membership one, and it leaks no team identity. Every CSRF 403 likewise stays.
steps.scenario_name: A workspace member who is not on the team cannot create a project there; A workspace member not on the team cannot file an issue against that team's project
steps.implementation_notes: BOUNDARY WIDENED after the first dispatch stopped correctly at it. Step-definition files us_07_project_create.rs, us_10_comments.rs and us_11_attachments.rs may be modified ONLY for the 403->404 assertion. Everything else under crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/ remains off-limits. Production work (20/20 call sites, 5 helpers deleted) is already COMPLETE from the first dispatch; this re-dispatch finishes the three scenarios it could not reach.

validation.notes: 34 DISTILL scenarios (all @pending, classified 29 RED / 5 expected-GREEN / 0 BROKEN) mapped to 10 steps in 3 phases; phase number = slice number, ordered 01 -> 02 -> 03. Slices 02 and 03 both depend on slice 01's issue_delete primitive; 02 and 03 are independent of each other. Steps 01-01 and 01-02 un-pend no acceptance scenario — they carry store/service integration tests only — because slice 01's learning hypothesis is about the primitive's transaction shape, which no acceptance scenario can isolate. Every one of the 34 scenarios is claimed by exactly one step; zero orphans. No migration: the schema head stays 0015. AUTOMATED GATE: PASS — step-id format, no validation-only steps, DISTILL linkage on every step, no AC coupling to private methods, decomposition ratio 0.71 (<2.5), no step covering 8+ scenarios (01-04 was split twice to clear the flag: happy path / refusals / no-JS). COVERAGE GATE: PASS — all 34 scenarios claimed by exactly one step, zero orphans, zero multi-claims. des-verify-integrity --roadmap-only exits 0. REVIEWER: not dispatched — the session forbids spawning agents; the automated gates above and a self-review stand in for @nw-acceptance-designer-reviewer, which is weaker than the wave specifies. Status stays pending_review rather than approved to keep that honest.
